subject: general
question: The President of India is elected by:
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Electoral College**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **President of India** is elected by an **Electoral College**.
 
• The **Electoral College** for the presidential election in India comprises:
 
• 
 
 
• **Elected Members of Parliament (MPs)** from both Houses (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha).
 
• **Elected Members of the Legislative Assemblies (MLAs)** of all Indian states and Union Territories with legislatures (like Delhi and Puducherry).
 
 
 
• This system is designed to provide a weighted representation from both the central and state governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Direct Election**: The President is not directly elected by the people.
 
• **System of Universal Adult Franchise**: This system is used to elect Members of Parliament and Members of Legislative Assemblies, not the President.
 
• **Members of the Parliament**: While MPs are part of the Electoral College, **MLAs** are also included, so it’s not limited to Parliament alone.
